mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (measured via 3-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months (5-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate profit expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and GDPC1 produces positive returns in less than 50% of instances (3-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During supply chain disruption regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing output contraction that reduces corporate margins and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines during supply chain disruption (5-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 jobs per month signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 100,000 jobs/month (3-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly Consumer Price Index acceleration exceeding 0.5% signals inflationary pressure that triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month (5-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent retail sales growth (RSAFS) and federal funds rate decline (FEDFUNDS) signal strong consumer demand combined with monetary easing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and falling FEDFUNDS produces positive returns in less than 50% of instances (3-year rolling window IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor market regimes, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor conditions that increase consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE declines during labor market tightness (5-year rolling window IC < 0.03).
